lines.meet: The name's Leif. I cut trees for a living back home, and out here I mostly don't.
lines.meet_neighbour: You're out at Dawnrest too. I'm the one stacking deadwood behind the waystation at first light.
lines.ask_home: Whereabouts is home for you, if you don't mind me asking?
lines.ask_work: What kind of work did you do back home? You don't have to say.
lines.answer_home: Coos Bay, on the Oregon coast. Fog, rain, big timber, and a mill on every second street.
lines.answer_work: Logging, twenty-five years in the Coast Range. I set chokers, then I fell trees, then I climbed them.
lines.chat_food: Black coffee out of a thermos, sitting on a stump at dawn with the fog still in the trees. That's about all I need.
lines.chat_sleep: I sleep okay as long as nothing dead is hanging over me. I check before I put my tent down.
lines.chat_missing: First light in a stand of old trees, when it's dead quiet and the fog's just lifting. I didn't know how much I'd miss that.
lines.chat_here: The woods out here woke up in me the week I came through. I cut down forests for a living, so I'm still working out what they meant by it.
lines.tease_quiet: You and me could go a whole day without a word, {name}, and I'd call it a good day.
lines.tease_talker: You'd scare every deer in three valleys, {name}. Not that I mind the company.
lines.tease_careful: You size things up like an old faller, {name}, and that's kept me alive more than once.
lines.tease_bold: You walk under things without looking up, {name}. One day I'm going to make you wear a hard hat.
lines.tease_any: You'd make a decent ground man, {name}, if you ever learned to stand still.
lines.tease_back: Well, you got me there, {name}, fair enough.
lines.take_it_kindly: Yep, that's true, {name}. Can't argue with it.
lines.bristle: Not that one, okay, {name}. I lost a friend to a falling limb.
lines.needle_quiet: If you see something coming down, you yell. Keeping quiet about it gets people killed.
lines.needle_talker: Every animal in these woods knows exactly where we are, thanks to you.
lines.needle_careful: You can look at a tree all day, but sooner or later somebody has to make the cut.
lines.needle_bold: You rush in without reading the ground, and the woods punish that every time.
lines.needle_any: You never look up, and up is where the things that kill you come from.
lines.bite_back: I've taken the big ones down every fight we've had. You don't get to say I don't carry my end.
lines.hurt: That one landed. I'll go sit with the trees for a bit.
lines.laugh_off: I've had a crew boss yell at me over a chainsaw for twenty years. You'll need to be louder than him.
lines.apologise: I was out of line there, and I'm sorry. I get short when I'm tired.
lines.double_down: Yep, I stand by it. Better you hear it from me than learn it the hard way.
lines.confide: {name}, my falling partner was killed by a dead branch out of a tree I was cutting. Everybody said it wasn't my fault.
lines.listen: Go slow, {name}. I'm a good listener, it's the talking I'm bad at.
lines.look_out: Stand where I tell you, {name}, and nowhere else. I've got the canopy.
lines.accept: Your call, {name}. You lead, and I'll back you.
lines.deflect: Walked off worse in the woods, {name}. Check on somebody else.
lines.check_in: You took a hit, {name}. Sit down a second and let me look.
lines.blame: Somebody stood where they shouldn't have, and it came down on all of us.
lines.thank: That was a bad spot, and you got me out. I owe you.
lines.brush_off: Don't mention it. Watching your back is the job.
lines.worry: Easy, {name}, easy. Stay down, I've got eyes on it.
lines.handed_down: This should be yours. Here, take it back.
lines.hand_fine: Sure, take it. I spent twenty-five years in gear held together with tape.
lines.hand_sulk: Didn't ask me, huh. Well, that's how it goes.
lines.turn_friendly: I'd let you be my ground man, {name}, and I don't say that to many people.
lines.turn_friends: I'd climb anything for you, {name}, and I'd trust you to watch the canopy while I did.
lines.turn_grating: You and I don't see eye to eye. That's okay, the work still gets done.
lines.turn_rivals: I'll still yell if something's coming down on you. Just don't expect much more than that.
lines.make_up: Look, {name}, let's call it even and start over. What do you say?
lines.defend: Back off, that's not right. {name} did exactly what they were told.
lines.friend_left: It's quiet without {name}, and I didn't think I'd mind quiet.
lines.friend_back: {name}, good to see you back. Feels right again.
lines.common_american: You sound like home. Whereabouts in the States? I haven't heard it in anybody's voice for a long time.
lines.common_wild: You know the wild places, I can tell by how you walk. You don't step on anything you don't have to.
lines.common_scandinavian: Up north, right? My grandfather came over from Norway, and he talked just like you do.
lines.common_parent: You've got kids. I can tell by how you count heads. I've got a daughter who fights wildfires, and I think about her a lot.
